derivationChain.quote: No canonical module count exists in the source for the Standards and Operations Studio; this blueprint derives a logical model of 18 modules from §5.1 to §5.18 and labels it `Derived Clarification`, carried as `DEC-STUDIO-001`. derivationChain.note: Contrast: DOH 19 SoW Fact §4.1.3, CC 13 SoW Fact §6.1.6, FL 12 SoW Fact §7.3, SA 19 capability sections §8.1-§8.19.

derivationChain.quote: The Statement of Work provides no canonical module count for the Standards and Operations Studio. Part V describes the Studio's scope in eighteen numbered sections (§5.1 through §5.18) but nowhere presents a module inventory table equivalent to §4.1.3 for the Delivery Operations Hub, §6.1.6 for the Client Command Center, or §7.3 for the Frontline Worker Application. Any Studio module count is therefore derived, not sourced. This is recorded as `DEC-STUDIO-001`.

The derivation rule used. One module per numbered section of Part V, in section order, with the section's own heading as the module name. This yields exactly eighteen modules, `MOD-STU-01` through `MOD-STU-18`.

Part V's numbered sections are already scoped by function, each with a distinct owner, a distinct object type, and distinct governance... A model that respects the source's own section boundaries is the model least likely to invent a seam the source does not have.

risks.risk: A build renders a published version as live on the floor.
risks.why: The Studio's whole publication surface is one step away from claiming a device state it cannot know. L31181: 'A published version is not in force on a device until the corresponding version-change command reaches applied on that device. The Studio's publication view must therefore never show a version as "live on the floor".' Three acceptance criteria guard it — AC-STU-023 (L31226), AC-STU-112 (L33590), AC-STU-118 (L33769) — and SB-STU-03 (L31304) writes the honest summary line: 'Published. One Job notified. Zero of one devices on this version.'
risks.mitigation: Every adoption figure renders in its true command state from the fifteen-state ladder; a gate plants a 'live on the floor' string and proves it red.

risks.risk: The Read-only Auditor column gets a status instead of a decision.
risks.why: DEC-AUDSTU-001 is open and touches 15 of the 26 matrices, and THREE places in the source already give the Auditor a status — §25.3 L48321 'Not applicable', §25.3 L48325 'Read-only', SEQ-010 L67908 'Read-only'. An implementer transcribing from any of those three will fill a cell the chapter deliberately leaves open. AC-STU-157 (L34674) is explicit: 'every Read-only Auditor cell states Client Decision Required'.
risks.mitigation: The token vocabulary carries `Client Decision Required` as a first-class rendering; a gate asserts no Auditor cell on SURF-STU resolves to a permission status.

risks.risk: A third inheritable default is added to the Workflow Builder.
risks.why: L32040: 'exactly two workflow-level defaults... The word "exactly" is the source's own and is load-bearing: an implementation that adds a third inheritable default, however convenient, departs from the specification and must be raised as a change request.' Severity is the obvious candidate and is the one thing forbidden — FUNC-STU-04-01-C-1 (L32094) makes the refusal a functionality, and AC-STU-055 (L32180) forbids the API route as well as the control.
risks.mitigation: The four settings and two defaults are a closed vocabulary with an exhaustiveness check; a gate plants a third default and proves it red.

risks.risk: The canvas drawing is treated as documentation rather than as the sequence-detection rule.
risks.why: L32042: 'The drawing is not documentation. It is the rule.' FUNC-STU-04-02-A-2 (L32098): 'no role may author a sequence reference that differs from the drawn order, because two references would make skip detection unfalsifiable.' A build that stores the drawn order and the detection reference separately creates exactly the second reference the source forbids.
risks.mitigation: One data structure; AC-STU-056 (L32181) as a gate that reads the built artefact.

risks.risk: A capture type outside the adopted seven is offered.
risks.why: TWO seven-type lists exist and differ. L32232: 'a Frontline player cannot render a type the contract does not name.' TEST-WF-AUT-002-04 (L53401) demands the check be a BUILD failure: 'Cross-check the Builder capture-type list against the Frontline renderer list and fail the build on divergence.'
risks.mitigation: One `as const satisfies readonly CaptureType[]` with an exhaustiveness check, named verbatim from AC-STU-065 (L32421), plus a gate that plants an eighth type.

risks.risk: A screen that can deviate publishes with no severity mapping.
risks.why: Stated four times: L32244 'the platform never assumes a value', AC-STU-042 (L31853), AC-STU-062 (L32418), AC-WF-AUT-002-01 (L53400), AC-SCR-STU-003 (L48348), AC-011-01 (L68168). It is the single most-restated rule on the surface, which is itself the signal that it is the one most likely to be got wrong.
risks.mitigation: A publication-blocking validation that names each unmapped screen; the gate plants an unmapped measurement screen.

risks.risk: The severity-1 arming confirmation is rendered as a warning rather than as a recorded act.
risks.why: FUNC-STU-05-08-C-1 (L32313) specific difference: 'if the confirmation cannot be recorded, the mapping is not saved.' AC-STU-043 (L31854) and AC-STU-063 (L32419) both require the CONFIRMATION to be recorded, not the warning to be shown. A build that shows the panel and saves regardless satisfies a naive reading and fails both criteria.
risks.mitigation: The confirmation is a write through the audit path; the covering test mutates the band before the audit fails and asserts the band did not persist.

risks.risk: Separation of duties is evaluated by role rather than by identity.
risks.why: L33389: 'A user holding both the Supervisor and Quality Manager roles is still one person and still cannot occupy two stages.' AC-STU-100 (L33400), AC-STU-153 (L34670), AC-SCR-STU-002 (L48347), TEST-STU-152 (L34681). A role-based check passes every test written with single-role personas and fails the one multi-role persona the source insists on.
risks.mitigation: Distinctness keys on identity; a fixture persona holds both roles and the gate asserts refusal.

risks.risk: A Studio view claims an escalation was delivered.
risks.why: AC-STU-028 (L31328): 'No Studio view reports escalation as delivered before the Delivery Operations Hub records delivery.' L31257: 'a tenant must never be told that an offline device "escalated"; the device classified and held, and the escalation was delivered when connectivity returned.' AC-STU-123 (L33944).
risks.mitigation: Escalation state renders from the notification-state ladder; no Studio surface holds a delivery claim.

risks.risk: The superseded discovery-stage description of offline severity evaluation reappears.
risks.why: L31256 and L33803 both name it explicitly, and AC-STU-030 (L31330) and AC-STU-126 (L33947) both forbid it: 'The superseded discovery-stage description of offline severity evaluation appears nowhere in delivered documentation or user interface text.' The superseded wording is 'processed at sync, with severity-band evaluation running on the captured value at that point'. It is a plausible sentence that an implementer might write from first principles.
risks.mitigation: A string gate over the built artefact for the superseded phrasing.

risks.risk: A Shared Instruction Block is modelled as a library item.
risks.why: L32443: 'A block is not a library item. It has no cross-Workflow reuse, no independent version number, and no separate governance: it lives inside its Workflow and is published, diffed, and archived with it.' AC-STU-066 (L32558). The natural data model for 'write once, apply to eight screens' is a library, and the source forbids exactly that.
risks.mitigation: The block record is keyed by Workflow; FUNC-STU-06-02-B-1 (L32486) refuses cross-Workflow reference at the service layer, and the gate attempts one.

risks.risk: The Studio mints a second audit log.
risks.why: L31481: 'The Studio keeps no audit log of its own. There is one immutable log per tenant, owned by the Delivery Operations Hub.' This is the same defect shape slice 4 named in its D14 — building a second store to make a slice self-contained, invisible until the owning slice tries to reconcile.
risks.mitigation: Read-through over slice 4's audit fixture; a gate asserts one store.

risks.risk: Two decision identifiers for the rollback question both get built.
risks.why: DEC-WFROLL-001 (chapter 28) and DEC-VERROLL-001 (chapter 7) ask the same question with no cross-reference. A census that reads both chapters will register two open decisions where the client has one.

risks.risk: A screen sentence points at content that is not there.
risks.why: Slice 4's defect shape 5, and this surface is dense with pointers: screens hold pointers to library items (AC-STU-071, L32763), a coaching default per declared locale (AC-STU-074, L32766), a certification the tenant maintains (L33664), a branch target (L32101), a block reference (L32483), a part reference (L33211). Every one of those is a sentence on a screen naming content elsewhere.
risks.mitigation: Every pointer-bearing sentence has a test that fails when its target is removed — not one that iterates an array and can only pass.

risks.risk: Scope is enforced in what a screen draws rather than in what it reads.
risks.why: Slice 4's defect shape 7. Here the scope dimension is not Site/Area but DRAFT VISIBILITY: L34508 'Drafts and in-review versions are visible only to grant-holders and the chain'. AC-STU-048 (L32013) and AC-STU-151 (L34668). A build that renders the Library from an unfiltered read and hides draft rows in the component has the same defect slice 4 shipped.
risks.mitigation: The selector filters; the component receives only what the identity may read; the gate asserts the selector, not the render.

risks.risk: A Lane-B patch is built under one reading of DEC-LANEB-001 while the approval chain is built under the other.
risks.why: AC-STU-097 (L33397) and AC-STU-138 (L34332) are both acceptance criteria and cannot both hold for a package-borne Lane-B value. AC-STU-104 (L33404) and AC-STU-143 (L34337) both require the tension to be SURFACED rather than implemented silently, which is the only instruction that binds both sides.
risks.mitigation: The conflict renders on screen with both readings and their locators; the pinned fixture holds both and neither is asserted as the source's answer.

risks.risk: The package manifest is asserted against the wrong count.
risks.why: FIVE content classes at L33791/AC-STU-120 versus SIX at AC-WF-AUT-009-01/TEST-WF-AUT-009-01. A gate written against either number will pass while contradicting a named acceptance criterion.
risks.mitigation: The manifest is a data structure quoting the five numbered classes verbatim, with the six-way split recorded as a second grouping of the same contents rather than as a different manifest.

risks.risk: The eighteen-module count is rendered without its derived qualifier.
risks.why: L4183 names this exact failure — 'derived-count leakage'. L14442 requires the count to render with 'derived count, not stated in the Statement of Work' beside the number and DEC-STUDIO-001 linked, and TEST-ROLE-1023 (L14497) asserts it. AC-STU-014 (L30992) forbids ANY document, screen or interface from presenting a Studio module count as a SoW fact — and that includes this census and this design.
risks.mitigation: Every place the number 18 appears on a Studio surface carries the qualifier; a gate scans the built artefact for a bare Studio count.

risks.risk: The Studio's notification surface is built without identifiers.
risks.why: Forty-one notification rows exist across the eighteen cards, none carrying a NOTIF-* identifier, and notifications.json holds zero Studio rows. A slice-10 reconciliation will find forty-one behaviours with no register entry. Slice 4 hit the same shape with AC identifiers that existed with no content (its R9).
risks.mitigation: Register the forty-one as derived rows with their card locators at census time rather than at slice 10.

risks.risk: The Studio is built as if it could ever be offline.
risks.why: Every module card has an Offline field and seventeen of eighteen say 'Unavailable — the Studio requires an active connection'. L31515 warns that where an offline STATUS appears it 'describes the Frontline consequence of a Studio configuration, not a Studio user's own experience, and the row says so'. A build that renders a Studio offline state satisfies the shared state contract and contradicts the surface.
